headline: Highest risk is medium: Haystack’s broad network/MCP surface can feed Taipy workflows, creating prompt-injection and data-flow risks; no direct evidence of shared writes or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack can call MCP servers and REST APIs, so it may ingest external or tool-returned content; Taipy is a data-engineering/runtime layer that could consume that output in workflows. No shared channel is explicitly documented, but the MCP bridge makes instruction-like content plausible, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF Haystack is configured to read MCP or REST responses as prompt text
IF Taipy workflows pass Haystack output into downstream parsing or templating
mitigations: Disable MCP endpoints not needed for the workflow
Add a strict content separator between tool output and instructions
Sanitize/strip markup before Taipy consumes Haystack output
Log and review first-run tool responses
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and may send retrieved content to external services, while Taipy has no declared egress and no touched data classes. The pair does not show a shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage risk exists mainly if operators route sensitive inputs through Haystack.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are indexed or retrieved through Haystack
IF Haystack forwards retrieved text to a third-party API
mitigations: Keep sensitive corpora out of Haystack indexes
Restrict Haystack egress to approved domains
Use redaction before retrieval results are exported
Verify Taipy never receives raw secrets in inputs
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack exposes network/MCP APIs, but Taipy’s profile shows no write, network, OAuth, or filesystem mutation surface. With no overlapping mutable resource or shared lock domain documented, a capability conflict pathway is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF Taipy is extended with write access to the same mutable resource as Haystack
mitigations: Keep Taipy read-only for shared resources
Avoid granting both agents the same API credentials
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieved answers or facts, and Taipy can orchestrate data workflows; if Taipy treats Haystack output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The profiles do not prove action-taking authority, so this is medium rather than high, but the default workflow integration risk is real.
conditions: IF Taipy uses Haystack output without verification
IF downstream Taipy steps transform Haystack text into reports, jobs, or decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step before downstream action
Require schema validation on Haystack outputs
Cross-check answers against a second source
Mark generated content as untrusted in Taipy
requires-engineering: add automated fact-verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only Haystack explicitly touches anonymous usage statistics; Taipy lists no regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention mismatch. No compliance breach pathway is evidenced from the profiles alone, so the pair is not shown to violate a specific control.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into Haystack or Taipy deployments
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair by default
Document retention settings before deployment
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
